## Video recovery priority (binding order)

Competitor video is strategically useful for secondary brand-strategy comparison, but is
**not mandatory** for the primary TALA claim-experience objective. `scripts/build_video_asset_manifest.py`
and any future recovery effort should prioritise in this order:

1. Permitted TALA official/product videos.
2. Other permitted TALA-relevant videos (e.g. creator-authorised content).
3. Official competitor videos, for secondary comparison only.
4. Open-license generic apparel videos, for method demonstration only.

The Video Package/Pipeline verdicts below are judged on **genuine temporal processing quality,
analytical relevance to the primary objective, provenance, and stated limitations** — never on
whether every competitor brand has an authorised local video. Coverage width across competitors
is not a PASS/FAIL gate.

## Text Package / Pipeline — PASS

193 documents across `official_claims_corpus.csv` (37), `customer_experience_corpus.csv` (95),
and `creator_strategy_corpus.csv` (61), all strong/medium evidence strength. TF-IDF, sentiment,
and sentence-embedding features built in Day 2 (`data/processed/{official_claim,customer_text}_features.csv`).

## Image Package / Pipeline — PASS

24 official catalog images, 6 per brand (TALA, Adanola, Girlfriend Collective, Oner Active),
collected from each brand's own public Shopify `products.json` endpoint
(`scripts/collect_official_product_media.py`, `src/collectors/official_media.py`). All 24
verified: readable local file, valid width/height, non-empty SHA-256 hash, source page URL,
direct asset URL, `rights_or_access_basis=official_direct_public_asset`. Zero duplicate URLs,
zero duplicate file hashes. No creator thumbnails are counted in this total — the manifest's
`image_role` distinguishes `official_catalog` from `creator_thumbnail`, and only the former
counts toward Image Package coverage.

## Video Package — PARTIAL / Video Pipeline — PASS

- **62 total `video_assets.csv` rows.** 61 are `rights_or_access_basis=platform_metadata_only`
  — YouTube/TikTok URLs discovered from verified creator posts. These are **video leads**, not
  video assets: no yt-dlp, no unofficial downloader, no stream extraction was used against
  YouTube/TikTok/Instagram. They are correctly excluded from every coverage count.
- **1 genuinely processed video** (`tala_video_001`, TALA — the primary-objective brand):
  downloaded directly from TALA's own Shopify CDN (an embedded `<source src=.mp4>` on a product
  page — a standard first-party asset, not a platform scrape). Validated with OpenCV (readable,
  44.7s duration, 9 genuinely distinct sampled frames at opening/quarter/half/three-quarter/
  closing/interval positions), with frame-level (brightness/contrast/saturation/edge-density/
  perceptual-hash/CLIP embedding) and temporal (inter-frame perceptual distance, scene-change-
  count proxy, motion-intensity proxy, visual-consistency score, opening-to-closing visual
  change) features computed (`data/processed/video_frame_features.csv`, `video_level_features.csv`).
- Route 1 (official page video) found embedded video on **TALA only** — Adanola, Girlfriend
  Collective, and Oner Active product pages (25 scanned each) had none. Route 2 (open license)
  found none. Route 3 (authorised local) has 0 files supplied.

**Video Pipeline: PASS.** The pipeline is judged on whether genuine temporal processing *works*,
not on how many videos currently feed it. 1/1 genuinely processed videos produced a full,
non-null temporal-feature row (100% reliability on the input it received) — that is a working
pipeline, demonstrated end to end, independent of asset count or brand breadth.

**Video Package: PARTIAL**, judged against the TALA-depth target (ideal: ≥4 processed TALA
videos), not competitor brand count:
- TALA (primary objective): 1/4 target processed videos.
- Competitor (secondary comparison, not required for PASS): 0 processed videos — **this alone
  does not fail the package.**
- **Remediation, in priority order:** (1) recover more permitted TALA official/product videos —
  place any not directly downloadable under `data/raw/authorised_video_assets/`; (2) other
  permitted TALA-relevant video (e.g. creator-authorised); (3) official competitor video for
  secondary comparison only; (4) open-license generic apparel video for method demonstration
  only. No yt-dlp/unofficial downloaders; no fabricated assets.
- `transcript_available`/`transcript_text`: 0/1 — no transcript exists for the processed video;
  `has_audio_stream` is `None` (unknown) because this environment has no system `ffprobe` binary
  (OpenCV's `VideoCapture` is video-only) — a documented limitation, not a fabricated `False`.

## Multimodal Reference Package — PARTIAL (Day 2.6A)

Populated via `scripts/collect_reference_package.py` → `scripts/process_reference_package.py`
(`data/interim/day2_6/multimodal_reference_assets.csv`). Discovery reused strong/medium Day 2
hydrated sources first, then probed common Shopify/WooCommerce policy slugs + sitemap.xml on
TALA's own domains, then used DuckDuckGo for discovery-only (never as content) with direct-fetch
verification for the 13-item requirement checklist. Competitor pages were probed lightly for
secondary comparison only.

**83 rows attempted, 74 verified** (`collected`/`already_available`; 54 strong, 20 medium):
TALA 54/63 verified, Adanola 8/8, Girlfriend Collective 7/7, Oner Active 5/5. 4 TALA pages
blocked (robots-disallowed or fetch failure), 1 duplicate.

**Two real bugs were found and fixed mid-collection, not glossed over:**
1. The sitemap crawler initially picked up **image file URLs** (`.webp`/`.png`), which got
   run through HTML text extraction and produced binary-garbage "text" that spuriously cleared
   the strong-evidence length threshold (107 of an initial 171 TALA rows were corrupted this
   way). Fixed with a Content-Type gate in `fetch_reference_document` (rejects any non-HTML/PDF
   response as `reference_status=irrelevant`) plus a binary-extension filter in sitemap parsing.
   The corrupted manifest was discarded and collection re-run from scratch.
2. The DDGS-fallback requirement checklist initially accepted **any** successfully fetched page
   as satisfying a requirement, regardless of whether its classified `reference_type` actually
   matched — e.g. a DDGS query for "size guide" landing on a `material_specification` page was
   being counted as satisfying the size-guide requirement. Fixed by requiring the fetched page's
   classified type to be in the requirement's compatible-type list before counting it as found.

**TALA 13-item requirement checklist: 7/13 found, verified, not fabricated:**

| Requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Sustainability or responsibility policy | **found** |
| Material/fabric composition | **found** |
| Size chart or measurement guidance | **found** |
| Fit guidance | **found** (via size guide) |
| Return/refund policy | **found** |
| Certification evidence or explicit certification status | **found** |
| Supplier or manufacturing disclosure | **found** |
| Product specifications | not_found |
| Garment-care or wash guidance | not_found |
| Quality/warranty policy, if one exists | not_found |
| Packaging policy | not_found |
| Emissions or environmental-impact disclosure | not_found |
| Public brand/visual guidance, if available | not_found — **not required for GO**; a private internal style guide's absence is a documented limitation, never a blocker |

Full detail (pages checked, discovery method per item): `outputs/tables/day2_6_tala_requirement_status.csv`.
Every `not_found` item retains its search record — nothing was invented or replaced with generic
industry information to close the gap.

**Reference type distribution** (verified rows): `other` 32, `sustainability_page` 23,
`material_specification` 9, `return_policy` 8, `size_guide` 6, `certification` 3,
`supplier_disclosure` 2. `other` covers individual WooCommerce product-listing pages, shipping
policy, terms of service, and FAQ — genuinely outside the 15-type controlled vocabulary, not a
classifier failure (verified by manual inspection of the "other" pages' URLs/titles).

**Processing output:** 353 reference-document chunks (`data/processed/reference_document_chunks.csv`,
section-aware, 250–500 word target with smaller chunks for size tables), 78 tables
(`data/processed/reference_tables.csv`; 40 `size_chart`, 38 `other`), 584 document images
(`data/processed/reference_images.csv`; decorative icons/logos excluded, certification badges
retained). No embeddings/vector store built (out of scope for this task).

**Reference Package GO/NO-GO** (`outputs/tables/day2_6_reference_package_readiness.csv`,
Part K criteria): **NO-GO — 1 of 10 criteria unmet.** Only "Garment-care or wash guidance" is
missing; every other mandatory item (sustainability, materials, sizing, return policy) is
verified, both "evidenced-or-documented-not-found" items (supplier, certification) are met, 353
chunks with provenance exist, ≥1 structured table was extracted where a source provided one, and
no search snippet was ever counted as a document. **This is one unmet requirement away from GO** —
not populated on next collection because TALA does not appear to publish a distinct public
care/wash-instructions page (its care copy, if any, is likely on product pages already visited
and would fall under `other`/`material_specification`, not a dedicated guide).

## Claim-evidence candidate layer — PARTIAL

`scripts/build_claim_multimodal_candidates.py` links the 37 verified official TALA claims
(`rag_usable=True`, `evidence_strength` in `{strong, medium}`) to candidate evidence in the other
modalities. **A bundle counts as "processed" as soon as it has ≥1 verified modality** — the old
all-or-nothing text+image+video requirement collapsed real partial evidence (e.g. text +
reference) down to zero, which was inaccurate. `outputs/tables/claim_evidence_bundle_summary.csv`
reports every combination separately:

| Bucket | Count / 37 |
|---|---|
| ≥1 verified evidence modality (genuinely "processed") | 21 |
| ≥2 eligible modalities | 16 |
| Text evidence | 21 |
| Image evidence | 3 |
| Eligible video evidence | 0 |
| Reference evidence | 16 |
| Text + image + video | 0 |
| Text + image + video + reference | 0 |
| Insufficient evidence (0 modalities) | 16 |

- **Text:** 21/37 claims matched ≥1 customer-experience/creator-strategy document (sentence-
  embedding cosine similarity ≥ 0.35, same brand, top 3).
- **Image:** 3/37 claims matched a TALA product image. Image/video matching is deliberately
  gated to `claim_category == 'materials'` — a catalog product photo can plausibly corroborate
  a materials claim, but nothing in a garment photo can corroborate a labour, manufacturing-
  process, packaging, emissions, or circularity claim, so those categories are never given a
  fabricated visual match regardless of CLIP score (see "RAG/candidate modality routing" below).
  Only the single best (top-1) match above a 0.27 cosine-similarity threshold is kept.
- **Video:** 0/37 claims matched the one processed TALA video (threshold 0.24, none cleared) —
  with only one video asset in the pool, this is a low-power, honest result, not a failure to
  implement the matcher.
- **Reference (Day 2.6A):** 16/37 claims matched, via the Part I hierarchy —
  `manufacturing` (8/8) and `materials` (7/7) claims matched almost entirely, `circularity` (1/1)
  matched, but `labour` (0/14), `other` (0/5), `emissions` (0/1), and `packaging` (0/1) claims
  matched none — `data/interim/day2_6/multimodal_reference_assets.csv` has verified evidence for
  sustainability/materials/sizing/returns/certification/supplier disclosure but not for
  labour-specific or emissions-specific content, so the category gate correctly refuses to match
  those claims to an unrelated reference document rather than force one. See
  `outputs/tables/day2_6_claim_reference_coverage.csv` and `data/processed/claim_reference_matches.csv`
  (16 rows: `match_method`, `match_score`, `category_gate_passed`, `match_explanation` per match).
- Every row carries `requires_human_validation=True` — this is a candidate layer, not a scored
  divergence assessment.

## Primary claim-evidence fusion readiness (minimum defensible bar)

Primary fusion does **not** require all 37 claims to carry every modality. The minimum
defensible bar (`scripts/audit_assignment_modalities.py::evaluate_primary_fusion_readiness`,
`outputs/tables/primary_fusion_readiness.csv`) is:

| Criterion | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Genuine text pipeline operating | MET | official/customer/creator corpora built and feature-extracted |
| Genuine image pipeline operating | MET | 24 verified official images processed |
| Genuine video pipeline operating (any count) | MET | 1 video with genuine temporal features — count is not the gate |
| Multimodal Reference Package populated (≥1 document) | MET | 74 verified reference documents (Day 2.6A) |
| Missing modalities explicitly tracked per bundle | MET | `missing_modalities` populated on every row |
| ≥5 TALA claims with ≥2 eligible evidence modalities | MET | 16 claims currently qualify (Day 2.6A) |
| ≥1 TALA claim with a defensible text+image+video bundle | **UNMET** | 0 claims currently qualify |

**Overall: NO-GO — 1 of 7 criteria unmet** (down from 3/7 before Day 2.6A). All three pipelines
genuinely work and the Reference Package + multi-modality-bundle bars are now cleared; the sole
remaining blocker is the video gate, which this task does not touch — at least one materials
claim needs a genuine video match, most likely by recovering 1–3 more permitted TALA videos
(more candidate frames/products raise the chance a real match clears the 0.24 threshold; the
threshold itself will not be lowered to force a match).

## Multimodal RAG readiness and modality-routing design

RAG is **not implemented yet** (out of scope for this audit pass). The binding design principle
for when it is built: **route each claim's retrieval to the modalities that are actually relevant
to it, never force an irrelevant modality in merely to look multimodal.**

- A responsibility/sustainability/labour claim should retrieve text, tables, certificates, and
  document images primarily — not an irrelevant product video.
- A fit, product-presentation, or movement claim may legitimately retrieve text, catalog images,
  and product/try-on video.
- This principle is already implemented, not just stated: `build_claim_multimodal_candidates.py`'s
  `VISUALLY_GROUNDABLE_CLAIM_CATEGORIES` gate (currently `{materials}`) is exactly this routing
  rule applied to the candidate-generation layer — TALA's claim categories today are
  `labour`, `manufacturing`, `materials`, `packaging`, `emissions`, `circularity`, `other`, none of
  which include a fit/movement category, so only `materials` claims are ever offered an
  image/video match. When RAG is built, its retriever must reuse this same category→modality
  routing table (extended with a reference-document route for certification/impact-report
  claims) rather than retrieving all modalities uniformly for every query.

**RAG verdict: NO-GO**, for the same underlying reason as fusion — video evidence depth is the
remaining blocker (Reference Package is no longer the blocker after Day 2.6A). Building RAG
before the video gate closes would let it silently over-rely on text/reference, defeating the
point of a multimodal prototype.

## Readiness-correction changelog (2026-09-18)

Corrected against an earlier draft of this audit that penalised the Video Package for
competitor-brand video absence and collapsed the claim-evidence layer to a strict
text+image+video-or-nothing count:
- Video Package/Pipeline status now keys off TALA depth and genuine-processing reliability, not
  competitor brand-count breadth (Video Pipeline moved PARTIAL → PASS).
- Claim-evidence layer now reports the full 9-bucket breakdown instead of a single all-or-nothing
  count; `evidence_strength_summary` in `claim_multimodal_evidence_candidates.csv` no longer
  labels a text+reference bundle "unusable".
- Fusion/RAG GO/NO-GO now uses the 7-criterion minimum-defensible bar above instead of "all 37
  claims fully multimodal" — verdict is still NO-GO today, but for three specific, closeable
  reasons rather than an undifferentiated shortfall.

## Day 2.6A changelog (2026-09-19): Multimodal Reference Package built

- Populated the Reference Package: 74 verified documents, 353 chunks, 78 tables, 584 document
  images (see "Multimodal Reference Package" section above). Multimodal Reference Package moved
  FAIL → PARTIAL; Claim-evidence candidate layer's ≥2-modality bundle count moved 3 → 16.
- Primary fusion readiness moved from 3/7 to 6/7 criteria met — the sole remaining blocker is the
  video gate (out of scope for this task, deliberately left untouched).
- Two real data-integrity bugs were caught and fixed during collection, not shipped: (1) binary
  image files being run through HTML text extraction and mislabelled as strong-evidence text
  (107 corrupted rows discarded, collection re-run clean), (2) DDGS-fallback requirement matches
  being accepted without checking the fetched page's classified type actually matched the
  requirement being searched for. Both are covered by regression tests in
  `tests/test_reference_collection.py`.
- Fixed an unrelated but consequential performance/reliability bug found while rebuilding claim
  candidates: `compute_semantic_similarity`/`get_sentence_embeddings` were reloading the
  sentence-transformers model from scratch on every call — calling this in a per-claim loop (37
  times) intermittently failed with `httpx.ReadError [WinError 10054]` from repeated HuggingFace
  Hub cache-validation requests. Fixed with a module-level model cache in `src/text_features.py`
  (same pattern already used for CLIP in `src/image_features.py`); rebuild time dropped from
  5+ minutes (with intermittent failures) to ~1m15s (reliable).
